correctness.rationale: An idempotent fixes its interval image pointwise; outside the interval monotonicity forces the respective endpoints, giving exactly the clamps. For a clamp on [a,b], commutation forces g(a),g(b) into [a,b]; monotonicity then handles all interior points. On the left, g(a)=a allows all a−1 binary steps anchored at a, while g(a)>a forces a constant tail; on the right g(b)=b is the corresponding free case. These tests are also sufficient and the tail lengths guarantee the ambient range bounds. Given g(a)=a+i, g(b)=a+j, the binomial coefficient counts the internal rises. Rank is one plus the total number of rises, giving the polynomial including h=1, where both tails are free. The baseline sum is h s^(h−1)−(h−1)z s^(h−2) for h≥2, with the single- and double-tail corrections as stated. For the OGF put w=xu, s=1+z, X=1/(1−x), Y=1/(1−xs); after summing the baseline and corrections the numerator over (1−sw)²(1−zw) is zw[X(1−zw)+(Y−X)(1−sw)]². The bracket equals (1−x−zw)/[(1−x)(1−xs)], proving the claimed expression. At u=z=1 the cancellation gives x/[(1−x)^3(1−2x)^2] with the stated coefficients. Summing the n−k allowed starting values over all binary strings of n−1 steps with k rises gives (n+1)2^(n−2) maps for n≥2, and there are n(n+1)/2 clamps, yielding the stated 32/n² asymptotic. Independently enumerated maps and actual compositions for n=1,…,9 matched every per-clamp polynomial and the aggregated OGF coefficientwise with both rank variables symbolic; replay /workspace/branches/06d52e3e-455c-4b1d-9232-20fdbfd08766/independent_check.py (outputs check_n5.txt and check_n9.txt).
